headline: RU students clash over football match, several injured
summary: A penalty shootout between the History and Clinical Psychology departments ended in violence at Rajshahi University stadium.
details: Several students were injured in a clash between students of two departments at Rajshahi University following an inter-department football match this afternoon.
The incident occurred at the university stadium after a round-of-16 match between the Department of History and Department of Clinical Psychology ended in a penalty shootout.
The match finished 1-1 in regulation time. History won the shootout, sparking tension among supporters over sledging and celebrations, which escalated into a physical clash.

Ahmed Sanaullah Rafsan, a history student, alleged that the clinical psychology department's goalkeeper and captain attacked a player. He claimed a defender, Abu Suaib Mohammad Jim, was hit on the head with a brick.
Hasan Zaman, a clinical psychology student, claimed sledging from the gallery led to the tension and alleged that someone from the gallery hit their goalkeeper with a brick.
Roksana Begum, acting director of the Department of Physical Education and Sports, confirmed that fighting broke out after the History department won.
University Proctor Professor Mahbubur Rahman called the incident "completely undesirable" and stated that discussions would be held with teachers, students and organisers to resolve the matter.

headline: 1,484 hospitalised in 24 hours as 5 more die of dengue
summary: Total deaths this year have risen to 176, with over 4,000 patients currently undergoing treatment across the country.
details: At least five dengue patients died and 1,484 others were hospitalised in a 24-hour period, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the five deaths, four were reported in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and one occurred in the Rangpur division.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths in Bangladesh this year has risen to 176, while total cases have reached 58,400.
Currently, 4,132 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country.
